reasoning: All six entries are exactly as cited in ducklib.py. Return-type mismatches (intp vs uint64 for idx_t): duckdb_column_count (:105), duckdb_data_chunk_get_column_count (:155), duckdb_data_chunk_get_size (:156), duckdb_row_count (:225). Argument-type mismatches: duckdb_data_chunk_get_vector second arg col_idx (:157 intp(intp,intp)), duckdb_validity_row_is_valid second arg row (:233 int8(intp,intp)). DuckDB's idx_t is typedef uint64_t (confirmed from DuckDB source; also implied by the project's own CLAUDE.md rule 'idx_t -> uint64_t -> uint64'). The inconsistency is real: sibling idx_t-returning functions at :216 (duckdb_nparams), :226 (duckdb_rows_changed), :227 (duckdb_struct_type_child_count), :188 (duckdb_get_list_size), :190 (duckdb_get_map_size), :77 (duckdb_array_type_array_size) all correctly use uint64. ABI impact: neutral on 64-bit (both intp/int64 and uint64 are 64-bit values, same register/stack representation). Practical severity is low because no miscompilation occurs and counts never exceed 2^63 in practice. However the numba typing footgun is real: numba promotes mixed int64/uint64 expressions to float64, so user @njit code mixing one of these intp-typed returns with a correctly-uint64-typed count (e.g. duckdb_data_chunk_get_size vs duckdb_get_list_size) silently widens to float64. Severity 'low' is correct.
